newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge dismisses Ecuadoran suit against Texaco.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge dismisses Ecuadoran suit against Texaco.

text.p: A U.S. federal judge dismissed a class-action suit brought against Texaco Inc for alleged environmental damage in Ecuador, saying the United States was not the appropriate forum for the case.
A group of Ecuadoran rainforest residents accused Texaco of failing to protect the environment during the company's 28-year tenure in Ecuador.

The plaintiffs filed their suit in White Plains, site of Texaco's headquarters, in an unsuccessful bid to prove that decisions on the firm's Ecuadoran operations were carried out in White Plains, not Quito, home of Texaco's Ecuadoran unit.
In a written opinion, Judge Jed Rakoff reinforced an earlier U.S. decision to dismiss the case on the same grounds.

The plaintiffs' failure to bring the case against Ecuador's state oil company Petroecuador and the Republic of Ecuador alongside Texaco was another cause for dismissal since these entities participated in the operations, Rakoff said.

Sovereign immunity protects these Ecuadoran parties from such action. Without them, a U.S. court ruling in favor of the Ecuadorans "would be unenforceable on its face, prejudicial to both present and absent parties, and an open invitation to an international political debacle," the judge said.
"We're obviously disappointed and we will be studying all options available to us," said Martin J. D'Urso, one of the attorneys for the plaintiffs.
"Among the options are commencing a new action abroad, filing an appeal, or both," D'Urso said.
Texaco officials, tied up in a separate race discrimination case, were unavailable for immediate comment.

Texaco operated in Ecuador from 1964 to 1992, producing a peak of 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil. In 1994, the company signed an accord to shut abandoned wells and pits and revegetate land. Work is due to be completed in December.
-- Patricia Garip New York Energy Desk 212-859-1625
